the packaging of cellular RNAs into HIV-1 is not sufficient for their encapsidation.
APO3G is encapsidated into HIV-1 by a mechanism that is distinct from the encapsidation process of cellular RNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
APO3G is packaged specifically into HIV-1 by virtue of its interaction with viral genomic RNA and not by its interaction with cellular RNA.
APO3G packaging is not a general property of cellular RNAs, but rather it requires the presence of a specific viral RNA, most likely the viral genomic RNA.
